evals.prompt: I'm writing a small C tokenizer library that other teams will embed. It must be leak-free even on error paths and must not force a specific allocator on its users. Sketch the C function signatures for initializing the tokenizer and for adding/producing tokens, and briefly explain the allocation approach.
assertions: The init and operation functions accept caller-provided storage (buffer pointer(s) plus a capacity) rather than calling malloc/calloc/realloc internally to allocate the token storage.
Operations return a status/error code (e.g. a 'full'/overflow status) when capacity is exceeded instead of growing or reallocating.

The design exposes or describes a way for the caller to determine the required buffer size (e.g. a size-query / *_req() function) rather than the library owning a returned allocation the caller must free.

evals.prompt: In my 64-bit C program I have a growable array, and many other structures store raw pointers directly to elements inside it. When the array exceeds capacity it reallocs and every one of those pointers dangles. I do not want to rewrite all those references. How should I change the array's storage so the pointers stay valid as it grows?
assertions: Recommends reserving a large virtual address range up front and committing pages on demand (reserve/commit) so the array's base never moves and never reallocs, keeping existing pointers valid.
States that reserving address space costs only address space / page-table entries, not physical RAM (physical cost is only the committed/touched pages).

evals.prompt: My engine has a per-frame arena that I reset at the end of every frame. I just added a feature that parses some asset data, allocates it from that same per-frame arena, and caches it to reuse across many later frames. Is this design sound?
assertions: Identifies that data allocated from the per-frame arena becomes a use-after-free once the arena is reset, because an arena reclaims everything at reset and cannot free/retain individual objects.
Advises allocating the longer-lived cached data from storage whose lifetime matches its use (a different/longer-lived allocator or arena), i.e. grouping/matching allocations by lifetime.

evals.prompt: Code review question: is there anything to improve about this C accessor used to fetch a node out of a graph? `node_t *get_node(graph_t *g, int i);` We've been hitting occasional double-frees around graph nodes.
assertions: Points out that returning a raw pointer leaves ownership ambiguous (whether the caller must free it), which is a likely cause of the double-free/leak.

Recommends making ownership explicit: return a handle/index, or use an explicit borrow/take naming convention, or document that the accessor returns a borrowed (non-owning) pointer that the caller must not free.
